title: Homeland Security Investigations' Operation Renewed Hope uses facial recognition and AI image enhancement to identify 311 probable child victims in cold cases
summary: U.S.-led investigators credited facial recognition, reported as Clearview AI, and AI image enhancement for leads in a 2023 operation that made 311 probable identifications of child abuse victims.
account: Operation Renewed Hope began on 17 July 2023. The Cyber Crimes Center of Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) hosted investigators from the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), the U.S. Marshals, Interpol, Europol and 13 foreign agencies. They reviewed series of child sexual abuse material in which the victims had not been identified. On 9 August 2023 U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) reported 311 probable identifications of previously unknown victims, 14 positive contacts and several confirmed rescues from active abuse. More than 100 leads went to field offices and 25 countries, and arrests had already been made in the United States and Canada. The ICE release does not mention artificial intelligence (AI). NBC News reports that HSI officials credited new facial recognition and artificial intelligence technology for fresh leads. Mike Prado of HSI described AI- or machine-learning-enhanced images as a starting point for investigation. Forbes reports that officials did not confirm Clearview or any specific program. On 24 August 2023 ABC (Australia) reported that the operation used Clearview AI's facial recognition alongside other techniques, citing Scott Anderson, an analyst with Queensland Police. Crikey reported on 25 January 2024 that the operation ran from 17 July to 4 August 2023. Drawing on internal police correspondence and a statement from the Australian Federal Police (AFP), Crikey reported that Australian case material was analyzed with Clearview AI, which the AFP was not allowed to use. HSI repeated the operation each year through 2026. ICE reports that Operation Renewed Hope III, from 24 February to 7 March 2025, positively identified 36 victims. ICE reports that Operation Renewed Hope IV, from 2 to 13 March 2026, produced more than 100 positive identifications. ICE counts more than 600 children identified and rescued across the four operations.
purpose: Identify previously unknown victims and offenders in seized child sexual abuse material so that children can be located and rescued.
system: Facial recognition (reported as Clearview AI) and AI/machine-learning image enhancement used in victim identification
developer: Clearview AI (reported by ABC, Forbes and Crikey; not confirmed by Homeland Security Investigations) and unnamed image-enhancement tools
deployer: Homeland Security Investigations (U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement), Cyber Crimes Center
domain: Child protection / online child sexual exploitation

brief: Operation Renewed Hope ran from 17 July 2023 into early August at the Cyber Crimes Center of Homeland Security Investigations (HSI). U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) reported 311 probable identifications of previously unknown child victims and several confirmed rescues from active abuse, and arrests had already been made in the United States and Canada.[1] The case bears on the argument over police use of facial recognition, and AI's part in it is hard to weigh. The ICE release does not mention AI. NBC News reported that new facial recognition and artificial intelligence technology had produced fresh leads in formerly cold cases. Mike Prado of HSI said that images enhanced with AI or machine learning can give investigators a starting point.[2] ABC News in Australia reported that Clearview AI's facial recognition was used, and Forbes reported that officials did not confirm Clearview or any specific program.[3] Crikey reported on 25 January 2024 that Australian case material had been analyzed with Clearview AI, which the Australian Federal Police was not allowed to use.[4] The outcomes are ICE's count, and no figure shows how many identifications came from the tools and how many from manual work. In a separate case in Finland, police were reportedly reprimanded after a unit of the National Bureau of Investigation allegedly used Clearview AI to identify potential abuse victims.

display.answer: The operational results come from the release by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) of 9 August 2023. The credit to facial recognition and AI comes from officials of Homeland Security Investigations quoted by NBC News. Forbes names Clearview AI on the word of unnamed sources. ABC names it on the word of a Queensland Police analyst. Crikey drew on internal police correspondence and an Australian Federal Police statement. The figures for the later operations come from ICE.
The geopolitical implications are unclear.

fields.summary: U.S.-led investigators credited facial recognition, reported as Clearview AI, and AI image enhancement for leads in a 2023 operation that made 311 probable identifications of child abuse victims.
fields.account: Operation Renewed Hope began on 17 July 2023. The Cyber Crimes Center of Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) hosted investigators from the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), the U.S. Marshals, Interpol, Europol and 13 foreign agencies. They reviewed series of child sexual abuse material in which the victims had not been identified. On 9 August 2023 U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) reported 311 probable identifications of previously unknown victims, 14 positive contacts and several confirmed rescues from active abuse. More than 100 leads went to field offices and 25 countries, and arrests had already been made in the United States and Canada. The ICE release does not mention artificial intelligence (AI). NBC News reports that HSI officials credited new facial recognition and artificial intelligence technology for fresh leads. Mike Prado of HSI described AI- or machine-learning-enhanced images as a starting point for investigation. Forbes reports that officials did not confirm Clearview or any specific program. On 24 August 2023 ABC (Australia) reported that the operation used Clearview AI's facial recognition alongside other techniques, citing Scott Anderson, an analyst with Queensland Police. Crikey reported on 25 January 2024 that the operation ran from 17 July to 4 August 2023. Drawing on internal police correspondence and a statement from the Australian Federal Police (AFP), Crikey reported that Australian case material was analyzed with Clearview AI, which the AFP was not allowed to use. HSI repeated the operation each year through 2026. ICE reports that Operation Renewed Hope III, from 24 February to 7 March 2025, positively identified 36 victims. ICE reports that Operation Renewed Hope IV, from 2 to 13 March 2026, produced more than 100 positive identifications. ICE counts more than 600 children identified and rescued across the four operations.
